name: Box Breathing
description: Inhale for four, hold for four, exhale for four, hold for four. A simple square that steadies the mind and body.
why: Used by martial artists and warriors to find calm under pressure. The even rhythm balances the nervous system and sharpens focus before training or rest.

name: Deep Dan Tian Breathing
subtitle: Abdominal · 6 · 2 · 6
description: Breathe low into the belly, letting the Dan Tian (a point two inches below the navel) rise and fall. Long, smooth, and silent.
why: The foundation of Shaolin internal practice. Deep abdominal breathing cultivates Qi, oxygenates fully, and roots the body — the source of relaxed power.

name: 4-7-8 Calming Breath
description: Inhale through the nose for four, hold for seven, exhale through the mouth for eight with a soft sigh.
why: A natural tranquiliser for the nervous system. The long exhale activates the parasympathetic 'rest and digest' response — excellent before sleep or to release tension.

name: Shaolin Energizing Breath
subtitle: Quick · 2 · 1 · 2
description: Brisk, rhythmic breathing to wake the body. Sharp inhale, brief hold, firm exhale — building heat and alertness.
why: A morning or pre-training warm-up. Faster cycling raises energy and circulation, clearing grogginess and preparing the body to move.
